apex_basket.thesis: Duerr builds the paint shops carmakers install and owns Homag, the largest woodworking-machinery maker; at EUR 16.40 it trades about 31% below a review-confirmed worth of EUR 23.75, valued on a sum-of-the-parts (each business valued separately) rather than on this year's disposal-inflated profit.
apex_basket.growth_durability: Weak: revenue down about 3% this year and returns on capital near 5%, and free cash flow turned negative (about EUR -39 million) in the September quarter; the case is a margin recovery and asset value, not growth.
apex_basket.decision_rationale: Held since 24 August 2026 at EUR 17.32 (now EUR 16.40, about 5% under water) and the thesis holds - the review confirmed every balance-sheet figure against the 30 September filing; graded wait for a better price, so not a buy here, with adds near EUR 15. Interest cover of about 0.6 times on reported profit means a further rise in borrowing costs and tighter car-industry capital budgets would delay the margin recovery the worth depends on, so it stays at 0.4 units.
skeptic_corrections: No load-bearing number moved. The bear case's balance-sheet inputs check out against FMP's 30 Sep 2026 quarterly balance sheet: net debt 240.1m euros (borrowings 987.2m less cash 747.2m), up from 218.1m on 30 Jun 2026; shareholders' equity 1,227m euros; market value 1,088m euros at 15.72 euros, which implies about 69.2m shares and matches the record's share count.

The free-cash-flow reversal checks out against FMP quarterly cash-flow statements: +103.5m (Q4 2025), +45.8m (Q1 2026), +12.6m (Q2 2026) and -39.0m (Q3 2026). Q3 net income was 4.9m euros and customer prepayments (deferred revenue) fell from 988.6m to 866.9m in the quarter. The screen's anchors (4.3 times free cash flow, 2.92 euros of earnings per share) are inflated by the disposal gain and the cash pulled forward, as the record already says. The base value of 23.75 does not rest on them.

Footnote: the balance sheet carries only 18.3m euros of minority interest, against the 80m HOMAG minority claim used in the adverse case. HOMAG's outside shareholders are probably carried under other liabilities (the domination-agreement compensation), so 80m is the conservative choice and is kept as it is.

Not verified: segment margins (Automotive 7-8%, HOMAG, Schenck), the 2026 guidance (free cash flow -150m to 0 euros) and the undisclosed tax-audit amount come only from the call transcripts in the dossier. They were not checked against the Q3 2026 statement on the company's IR site, because this turn's web-search budget was used up and FMP returned no news for 15 Oct to 16 Nov 2026.
apex_basket.cro_wait_quote: Wait for a better price: we buy near 15.00 euros, which the sector sell-off could deliver. The thesis holds, and the third quarter reported on 12 November 2026 supported it: orders up 5%, sales up 3%, Automotive sales up 15% with a margin above last year's strong 8.2%, the group margin before one-off items at 5.7% (the best of the year), and full-year guidance confirmed.

apex_basket.thesis: Inchcape distributes and retails cars for Toyota, Jaguar Land Rover and other makers, mostly outside the UK, and at 651 pence trades about 30% below a re-debated worth of 930 pence, though Asia-Pacific volumes are falling sharply.
apex_basket.growth_durability: Weak near term: revenue down about 2%, the margin guide cut to about 5.5% on 22 October and statutory profit falling faster than the adjusted figure; returns on capital near 10% and cash conversion above 100%.
apex_basket.decision_rationale: Held since 13 October 2026 at 674.5 pence (now 651 pence, about 3% under water); re-debated in full today, the debate still grades it buy now and the worth moved from 950 to 930 pence, which takes in the second model's repricing. Inchcape funds about GBP 2 billion of car inventory with borrowings and covers interest only about 2.4 times, so a further rise in borrowing costs and tighter car credit would squeeze a 5% margin - it stays at 0.4 units.
skeptic_corrections: No load-bearing number moved. Net debt 674m GBP (incl. 275m non-current leases) and minorities 73m GBP verify exactly against the 2026-06-30 balance sheet; the 332.2m share count reconciles to FMP market cap 2,137.8m GBP / 643.5p. Note the 674m is a June print on a seasonal working-capital book (FY2025 year-end was 607m) and does not yet carry the rest of the 250m GBP buyback, so the per-share sensitivity runs both ways and nets roughly flat.

Bear pressure that survives but is NOT a kill: statutory earnings are deteriorating faster than adjusted (FY2025 statutory PBT 406m vs operating income 540m, interest expense up from 157m to 195m GBP y/y on ~2.0bn GBP of inventory). The base case must be read on ~10% guided 2026 adjusted EPS growth that is itself buyback-driven, not operating-profit-driven (FY2025 statutory EBIT 540m vs 611m in FY2024).

Unquantified UK motor-finance indemnity (FCA redress scheme live 2026-03-31) remains a hidden-disqualifier candidate; the record's 75m GBP bear provision is an estimate, not a disclosure, and no primary-source quantification was found. It is a sizing risk, not a verified kill.

Catalyst is SOFT (2026-11-19 investor webinar, buyback); do not treat as hard. Q3-2026 trading update facts (APAC volumes -37%, margin guide ~5.5%, EPS growth ~10%) could not be re-verified against the primary RNS in this pass (web search budget exhausted); they come from the dossier's secondary coverage.

apex_basket.thesis: Kia is a profitable, still-growing carmaker holding about 21 trillion won of net cash (roughly 54,500 won a share, more than half the share price), and at 94,600 won it trades about 30% below a worth of 135,000 won that already haircuts consensus earnings and credits the cash at only two-thirds.
apex_basket.growth_durability: Moderate: revenue up about 10% and operating profit up about 24% in the September quarter, three-year revenue growth near 10% a year and returns on capital near 11%; gross margin is eroding under the new US tariff, and net income fell about 10% on an unexplained drop in below-the-line income.
apex_basket.decision_rationale: Never held; graded buy now on a full debate seven days old, all five valuation models call it cheap, and at a 42.7% discount it clears the 29.0% median bar of the held seats - it is the third car-cycle leg, so the three share a combined cap of 1.3 units. Kia carries no borrowings, but higher rates and tighter US auto-loan credit would hit its unit demand, which is part of why it is a half unit.
skeptic_corrections: risk_reward cites a live price of 97,000 won; FMP quote on 2026-11-16 is 95,000 won (52-week range 87,900-212,500; 50d avg 111,362, 200d avg 142,958). Footnote only: the levels (bear 80,000 / base 135,000) are unchanged and the pipeline recomputes ratios from live price.

The bear SoP credits only net cash (about 21.2T won = cash 16.08T + short-term investments 7.37T - total debt 2.25T at 2026-06-30, about 54,300 won/share on 390.0M shares; 60% = about 32,600) and ignores 30.1T won of long-term investments (affiliate stakes). The 80,000 bear level is therefore conservative, not stale; no level moved.

Unresolved risk, not a kill: Q3 2026 below-the-line income collapsed to 3.9bn won (vs 430-440bn won in Q1/Q2 2026 and 425bn in Q3 2025), so net income fell to 1.286T won (-9.8% y/y vs 1.425T) while operating income rose to 1.818T (+24% y/y vs 1.462T). FMP's Q3 line items are partial (no cost/interest breakdown), so the cause (equity-method loss, FX, impairment) could not be verified from a primary filing; if it is a recurring affiliate loss, the earnings anchor should be re-checked at the next debate.

apex_basket.thesis: JD Logistics runs one of China's largest warehouse and delivery networks with revenue growing about 19% a year and net cash excluding leases, and at HK$10.27 it trades about 26% below a re-debated worth of HK$13.86, with a conservative downside case of HK$7.78.
apex_basket.growth_durability: Durable growth: revenue up about 19% this year and about 16% a year over three years; the review puts the return on equity near 13%, though gross margin slipped about a point in the June quarter and returns after lease costs are thin.
apex_basket.decision_rationale: Held since 20 October 2026 at HK$10.26 (now HK$10.27, flat); re-debated in full today, the debate still grades it buy now after cutting the worth from HK$15.0 to HK$13.86, which takes in the second model's repricing; the third-quarter results on 17 November are the next test of the margin path, so it stays at half a unit.
skeptic_corrections: Bear thesis 'return on invested capital about 1%' does not reconcile with the filed numbers: TTM IFRS net income RMB 7.36B (Q3-25 2.03 + Q4-25 2.04 + Q1-26 0.88 + Q2-26 2.41) on shareholders' equity RMB 56.83B (2026-06-30) is ~13% ROE; even on equity plus RMB 23.9B debt-and-leases the after-tax return is high single digits. The ~1% figure is a data-feed ratio artifact, not a fact. Footnote only - no valuation level depends on it.
ISC external-customer growth is quoted as 12.5% in the bear thesis and 12.1% in the dossier for Q2 2026; immaterial either way.
The bear case gives no credit for RMB 16.25B of long-term investments on the 2026-06-30 balance sheet; this makes HK$7.78 conservative, not wrong - left unchanged.

Load-bearing inputs verify: Q2 2026 revenue RMB 64.10B (+24.3% y/y vs 51.56B), gross margin 9.73% vs 10.63% (-0.9pp), cash+ST investments RMB 22.47B, borrowings RMB 5.17B, lease liabilities RMB 18.70B -> net debt after leases ~RMB 1.40B, diluted shares 6.404B. Bear arithmetic (RMB 6.5B x 6.5 / 6.404B x 1.1794 = HK$7.78) is internally consistent.
Timing risk, not a kill: Q3 2026 results print 2026-11-17 (tomorrow); the thesis is exposed to a binary read on margin trajectory. Catalyst correctly labelled SOFT_EXTENDED, not hard.

apex_basket.thesis: SoftwareOne resells Microsoft and other cloud software to about 70,000 companies and, after merging with Crayon, earns about a 24% adjusted operating-profit margin with CHF 100 million of cost savings already banked, and at CHF 8.72 it trades about 27% below a review-checked worth of about CHF 11.89.
apex_basket.growth_durability: Moderate but slowing: like-for-like growth of 7.4% in the third quarter after 11.6% in the first half, the margin guide raised to above 24%, returns on capital near 11% but falling and gross margin eroding as Microsoft trims partner incentives.
apex_basket.decision_rationale: Never held; graded buy now on a full debate dated today and at a 36.4% discount it clears the 32.0% median bar once Kia is seated, but it is seated on the margin of safety alone at 0.4 units: its downside case sits close to the price, only two of five models agree it is cheap, and returns are falling. It carries about CHF 483 million of real net debt on floating-rate loans with interest cover near 4 times, so further rises in borrowing costs come straight out of profit (interest expense was already up about 70% in the first half).
skeptic_corrections: Share denominator: the record's levels divide equity by ~214.5m basic shares (CHF 1,630m / CHF 7.60). The H1 2026 statement shows 217.06m weighted diluted shares (215.58m basic). On the diluted count the bear case is ~CHF 7.51, base ~CHF 11.89, bull ~CHF 14.33 (about -1.2%). Footnote-level; the arithmetic is otherwise intact.

Cash flow on the statement basis is softer than the CHF ~200m company figure: H2 2025 FCF CHF 146.1m + H1 2026 FCF CHF 28.1m (operating cash flow CHF 64.6m less capex CHF 36.5m, after a CHF 79.4m working-capital outflow) = ~CHF 174m over the last twelve months. This supports the bear's 'pass-through working capital is not free cash' point but does not move a valuation level, because the record values the business on EBITDA multiples.

Financing cost is rising: H1 2026 interest expense was CHF 31.9m (net CHF -26.1m), against CHF 18.9m in H1 2025, on CHF 865.8m of gross debt (CHF 310.8m short-term, CHF 555.0m long-term). This is consistent with the bear's floating-rate term-loan point; no level change.

Verified as stated: net debt CHF 483.0m at 2026-06-30 (debt CHF 865.8m less cash CHF 382.8m); pass-through receivables of CHF 4.52bn against payables of CHF 4.52bn; H1 2026 net income CHF 54.3m; price CHF 8.78, 52-week low CHF 5.83, market cap CHF 1.886bn. The Q3 2026 trading-update figures (7.4% like-for-like growth, channel +7.3%, margin guide raised to above 24%) could not be independently re-checked in this pass because the web-search budget was exhausted and FMP had no Q3 data for this semiannual reporter. They rest on the dossier.

apex_basket.thesis: Deckers owns the HOKA running and UGG footwear brands, earns about 28% on its capital with about $670 million of net cash after leases, and at $86.82 trades about 22% below a review-verified worth of $112 that already reflects the 22 October sales-outlook cut.
apex_basket.growth_durability: Durable growth: revenue up about 10% this year and about 15% a year over three years, gross margin near 58% and returns near 28%; September-quarter sales grew only about 3.5%, which the worth already reflects.

wheel.rationale: A net-cash, high-return brand owner with no dated catalyst re-rates slowly, so selling the put at the $72 downside case pays a premium while waiting and only assigns at a price where the upside to worth is about 55%.

apex_basket.decision_rationale: Held since 3 November 2026 at $84.09 (now $86.82, about 3% ahead); the debate still grades it buy now and the review confirmed every figure against the 29 October filing, but its downside case now sits only about 14-17% below the price, so it is held on the margin of safety alone and cut from 0.75 to 0.5 units.
apex_basket.skeptic_corrections: No load-bearing number moved. Verified against the FQ2 FY27 10-Q (filed 2026-10-29): net cash $0.67B (cash $1,209.7M less $539.5M lease liabilities, zero funded debt) and period-end shares about 133.7M (common stock $1.337M at $0.01 par) match the record's $0.67B and about 133.5M. Revenue $1,480.6M vs $1,430.8M = +3.5% y/y, as the bear states. TTM operating income is about $1.32B (389.5 + 155.3 + 156.7 + 614.4), so the bear's -20% to about $1.05B and the $72 bear price recompute correctly (1.05B x 8.5 + 0.67B over 133.7M = about $71.8). At $83.39 the EV of about $10.5B is already about 7.9x TTM operating income, near the bear multiple: much of the de-rating is priced in. Unverified here: the size of the one-off tariff refunds that flatter TTM earnings (the bear's own adjustment, about $0.29/share) - if larger, the base anchor is modestly high, but not enough to break the thesis. No litigation, covenant, dilution or regulatory disqualifier found; buybacks are shrinking the share count (diluted 148.6M to 135.3M y/y). Catalyst is SOFT_EXTENDED (no hard dated event), so the thesis rests on valuation, not a catalyst.

apex_basket.thesis: Stride runs the largest network of online public schools in the United States with about $264 million of net cash after its convertible and leases, and at $75.82 it trades about 23% below a worth of $99 that assumes enrollment stops falling.
apex_basket.growth_durability: Mixed: three-year revenue growth of about 11% a year and returns on capital near 11%, but count-date enrollment fell about 2.8%, adjusted operating income slipped in the September quarter, and management says AI-driven search is hurting new-student leads.
apex_basket.entry_posture: on_confirmation: Fiscal Q2 2027 results (expected around 2027-01-26): enrollment of 243,000 or more versus the 241,000 September count, with full-year adjusted operating income guidance held at $505M or more
apex_basket.cro_add_event: Fiscal Q2 2027 results (expected around 2027-01-26): enrollment of 243,000 or more versus the 241,000 September count, with full-year adjusted operating income guidance held at $505M or more
apex_basket.decision_rationale: Held since 10 August 2026 at $82.51 (now $75.82, about 8% under water); the thesis is in doubt but not broken - the review found no kill and the $60 downside case sits well below the price - so it is held, not added, until the late-January results show enrollment of 243,000 or more with the operating-income guide held at $505 million or more.
apex_basket.skeptic_kill_fact: No kill fact found. The bear facts verify against the Q1 FY27 primary record: enrollment of 241K vs 248K y/y (-2.8%), General Education down a little over 6% (Lone Star loss of about 3K students, Texas Alt-Ed capacity), Career Learning growth slowing, applications down, management confirming that consumer AI/Google search is hurting leads, full-year gross margin guided down 100-200bp, and the $420M convert due Sept 2027 with principal settled in cash. Even so, management guided FY27 adjusted operating income of $505-513M (Q1 adj OI of $78.6M vs $81.1M) and enrollment growing within the year since the count date. At $76.83 the EV of roughly $2.85-3.0B is about 6x adjusted OI, so the stock is already priced as the ex-growth contractor the bear describes. The $59 bear case sits only about 23% below the price and has no thesis-breaking disqualifier attached. The activist cooperation agreement (Fivespan, 2026-10-09) plus a new capital-allocation committee works against the bear, not for it.
skeptic_corrections: FY27 operating profit after stock pay is flattered by forfeitures: Q1 SBC was a BENEFIT of $7.4M and FY27 SBC is guided at $15-19M against about $41-43M in FY26. On a normalized run-rate, stock pay is about $25M higher, which takes about $0.4-0.5/share off a value built at 8x OI. This is footnote-level relative to the $97.5 base case, so no level moves.

Liquidity is $884.2M of cash plus marketable securities at 2026-09-30 per management (the FMP balance sheet shows $789M current, with the rest held as long-term securities). After the $420M cash settlement that leaves about $464M, or about $264M net of $200.6M of lease liabilities. The bear's 'about $320M net cash' falls between these and is acceptable.
Diluted share count was 44.83M in Q1 FY27 (basic 41.48M), consistent with the record's about 45M.
apex_basket.cro_add_event_director: Fiscal Q2 2027 results (expected around 2027-01-26): enrollment of 243,000 or more versus the 241,000 September count, with full-year adjusted operating income guidance held at $505M or more

thesis_test.metric: Total enrollment reported with fiscal Q2 2027 results (the December 2026 quarter), versus the 241,000 count on 2026-09-30, together with full-year fiscal 2027 adjusted operating income guidance
thesis_test.pass_level: Enrollment of 243,000 or more (positive in-year growth over the count date) and full-year adjusted operating income guidance held at $505M or more
thesis_test.fail_level: Enrollment below 241,000 (in-year decline, as in fiscal 2026) or full-year adjusted operating income guidance cut below $490M

apex_basket.cro_wait_quote: Wait for proof: we buy once fiscal Q2 2027 enrollment shows in-year growth above the 241,000 September count (243,000 or more) with full-year profit guidance held, due around 2027-01-26. The thesis is in doubt until that test. On 2026-10-19 this committee said the thesis held and that we would buy near $70 in a sector-wide or style-wide sell-off.

apex_basket.thesis: Tencent Music runs China's largest paid music-subscription service with about RMB 13.8 billion of net cash, and at HK$34.98 it trades about 19% below a worth of about HK$43 built on clean earnings (excluding interest income) plus that cash.
apex_basket.growth_durability: Moderate: second-quarter revenue grew about 6% with net income up about 3%; three-year revenue growth about 4% a year, and the debt-funded Ximalaya purchase dilutes margins.
apex_basket.entry_posture: on_confirmation: Third-quarter 2026 results, 2026-11-17 (announced by the company 2026-10-13, before the US market opens)
apex_basket.cro_add_event: Third-quarter 2026 results, 2026-11-17 (announced by the company 2026-10-13, before the US market opens)
apex_basket.decision_rationale: Held since 31 August 2026 at HK$34.12 (now HK$34.98, about 3% ahead); graded wait for proof, so not a buy here - it is held at 0.4 units until the third-quarter results on 17 November show revenue growth of 5% or more, gross margin no more than about 1.5 points lower and the company still in net cash.
skeptic_corrections: No load-bearing number moved. Every bear-side figure re-verified against the 6-K quarterly statements (via FMP): Q1-25 operating income RMB4,836m vs gross profit RMB3,242m (the one-off gain is real, so the cheapness must be measured ex-gain, as the record already does); Q1-26 revenue +6.7% y/y (7,847 vs 7,356) and Q2-26 +5.8% (8,933 vs 8,442); Q2-26 net income +2.6% (2,471 vs 2,409); goodwill 20.45bn -> 29.76bn (+RMB9.3bn, Ximalaya); total debt 4.82bn -> 16.88bn; weighted diluted ADS 1,551m (Q2-25) -> 1,556m (Q2-26), so the buyback shrank nothing. Trailing four-quarter net income Q3-25..Q2-26 = RMB8.60bn, matching the record's anchor.

Net cash at 2026-06-30 = cash RMB23.70bn + short-term investments 6.96bn - debt 16.88bn = RMB13.77bn, matching the record's RMB13.8bn. The US$1bn notes raised 2026-09-10 add debt AND cash, so they are net-cash-neutral until the cash is deployed; they are post-balance-sheet and not yet visible in a filed statement.

Share count: 3.11bn diluted ordinary shares = 1,556m diluted ADS x 2 ordinary per ADS - verifies; it is above FMP's HK-line implied count (HK$102.4bn mcap / HK$35.84 = 2.86bn), so the record is conservative here, not flattered.

Not a stale anchor: the trailing earnings window (Q3-25..Q2-26) excludes the Q1-25 non-operating gain. The FMP Q4-25 row (cost of revenue RMB176m, gross profit RMB7.57bn) is a corrupt data row and must not be used as a margin anchor; net income in that row (RMB1.90bn) is consistent with the other quarters.

Unpriced binary: Q3-26 results land 2026-11-17 (pre-US-open), one day after this review. The record's own bear-confirmation tests (revenue growth <= Q2's with Ximalaya fully consolidated, gross margin < ~43%, further acquisition spend) are all live on that print; the seat should be re-checked against it rather than treated as settled. Q2-26 gross margin was 44.2% (3,949/8,933), down only ~0.2pp y/y from 44.4%.

apex_basket.thesis: Morgan Sindall is a British builder and office fit-out contractor with about GBP 418 million of net cash and the best returns on capital among UK contractors (about 14%), and at 4,510 pence it trades about 9% below a worth of 4,955 pence.
apex_basket.growth_durability: Durable growth: revenue up about 10% this year and about 12% a year over three years with rising returns; the 5 November update guided the year slightly ahead, though the housing arm is now below expectations.
apex_basket.decision_rationale: Held since 27 October 2026 at 4,054 pence (now 4,510 pence, about 11% ahead); the thesis holds, but the price sits above its trim line (85% of fair value) and the debate now grades it wait for a better price, so it is held, not a buy here, with adds only near 4,129 pence - it is the first seat to give up if a stronger name needs the room.
skeptic_corrections: No load-bearing number moved. Group-level anchors in the adverse schedule check out against the H1 2026 balance sheet and income statement (FMP, period ending 30 Jun 2026): cash GBP 491.6m against GBP 97.5m short-term debt, which includes current leases. At 4,452p against a 4,955p base the discount to fair value is about 10%, short of the 20% entry floor. That is an entry bar, not a reason to kill the thesis.

grade_rederived.why: the expected return of 11.3% is below the 20% entry bar - wait for a better price, near 4,129

apex_basket.cro_wait_quote: Wait for a better price: we buy near 4,129p, which a thin-stock institutional sale could deliver. The thesis holds and the committee's numbers are unchanged. value_memo:
How this book was graded. Four tests carry roughly equal weight, about a quarter each. First, the margin of safety: how far today's price sits below the worth our chief risk officer (the seat that reconciles the bull and bear valuations into one number) reached after the bull-versus-bear debate, cross-checked against how many of five independent valuation models also call the name cheap. Second, whether the latest earnings are a cycle high already rolling over, in which case a low multiple is fake cheapness and the business is valued on mid-cycle profit instead. Third, solvency measured on interest-bearing borrowings only, not on the raw bankruptcy score, which over-penalises businesses that hold customer float or insurance reserves. Fourth, the multiple against true peers together with the durability of growth and returns: a low price on a business whose returns are falling and margins shrinking is a trap, not a bargain. A live catalyst is neither a plus nor a requirement. Those four tests, the hard limits and the hidden-factor stress decide who is eligible; eligible names are then taken in order of their discount to reconciled worth, because the 12 November reliability review found the grade score did not rank outcomes while the size of the discount did.

Book size. Nine names this week, up from seven: all seven held seats are kept and two are added. The bar for a new seat is the median discount of the seats already held - 29.0% before any addition (the seven held seats run from Morgan Sindall at 9.9% to Duerr at 44.8%). Taking eligible buy-now names in order of discount: Geely (0175.HK, 52.9%) is passed over on the correlation stress (below); JD.com (9618.HK, 49.5%) is out on the review's moat finding; Kia (000270.KS, 42.7%) clears 29.0% and is added, which lifts the median to 32.0%; SoftwareOne (SWON.SW, 36.4%) clears 32.0% and is added, which lifts it to 35.0%. The next buy-now names - Playtech (out on the review), PICC (31.0%), Dycom (29.1%) and everything below them - sit under 35.0%, so the book stops at nine. Nine names earn their place; a tenth would dilute every seat for a smaller discount than the median one.

What the forensic gate removed or capped. Thirty names are ineligible because the deep dive on management found a credibility red flag, among them BellRing Brands, Gartner, Molina Healthcare, Whirlpool, The Trade Desk, Corcept, Innoviva, Hub Group, Kyndryl, Super Micro Computer, Teleperformance, Corteva, Peabody Energy, Dream Finders Homes and Icahn Enterprises. Twenty more carry the worsening-trajectory cap, which holds their grade to about 50 and keeps every one out of the book; the largest optical discounts in that group belong to Great Wall Motor (about 51%), Gentex (28%), Visteon (19%), Pluxee (22%), Sprouts Farmers Market (23%) and Alnylam (14%).

Names the price-and-arithmetic check removed. Seventeen records do not reconcile with the live quote and are ineligible, among them Universal Health Services, Abercrombie & Fitch, Enphase, Equinor, Eiffage, Centrus Energy, Molina Healthcare and Icahn Enterprises; none is held. Eight names carry a downside case within 5-15% of the price, so the downside is not a real floor. Two of them are seated, each on its margin of safety alone and never on a risk-to-reward figure, and each at no more than half a unit: Deckers (DECK), held and cut from 0.75 to 0.5 units, and SoftwareOne (SWON.SW), added at 0.4 units. The others - Booking Holdings, Mixue, Boyd Gaming, KWS Saat, Rai Way and a Madrid-listed property company - are not seated. One more name (AEGN.AT, Athens) is ineligible because the nightly scan does not cover it, so its moat, payback and floor checks cannot run. Nine names fall below the 15% free-float floor and cannot be seated, including Christian Dior, Smithfield Foods, Icahn Enterprises and Electricite de Strasbourg.

Cyclical-peak and stale-earnings artifacts. BellRing Brands (BRBR), one of the two standing examples of this failure, shows about 161% upside on the raw screen but no reconciled worth this week: the debate grades it pass for now with the lowest value conviction, the screen is built on protein-shake earnings already rolling over (last full year 1.68 a share against 1.42 trailing), and it is ineligible on its credibility red flag in any case. Cal-Maine Foods (CALM), the other (egg-windfall earnings, now down sharply year on year), is back in the pool: its reconciled worth is $76 against $66.45 (about 14% upside) against about 49% on the raw screen, and it is graded wait for a better price near $63 and sits above its trim line - passed over. Other clear fake-cheap cases where the screen collapses once earnings are normalised: Boyd Gaming (about 445% on the screen against 19% reconciled), Great Wall Motor (178% against 51%), Mennica (298% against -20%), Valaris (112% against -6%) and PICC Group (78% against 31%, and the review found the anchor stale after a third-quarter loss). Inside the book, Duerr (DUE.DE) is valued on its sum-of-the-parts rather than its disposal-inflated profit (126% on the screen against a reconciled 45%) and Tencent Music (1698.HK) on clean earnings excluding interest income (130% against 23%). Kia (000270.KS) is a car maker, so its earnings well above the multi-year base are treated as cyclical: the worth uses haircut consensus operating earnings at 5.5 times plus two-thirds of its net cash, and even recession-level earnings (about 12,000 won a share, the 2021 level) at that multiple plus the same cash credit give about 102,500 won, still above today's 94,600 won - the cheapness survives normalisation. Deckers, JD Logistics, Morgan Sindall and Stride show earnings well above their multi-year base, but each is still growing revenue with healthy or rising returns and no earnings roll-over, so that is durable growth rather than a cycle peak.

What the adversarial review removed. The independent challenge ran before this allocation; each name below is out on its findings, not on grade:
- JD.com (9618.HK, graded buy now, 49.5% discount) did not hold up on competitive position: group returns sit below the cost of capital (about 0.6% on invested capital in 2025, perhaps 5-6% after tax on the recovered 2026 run-rate) with no primary-source proof they are durably rising. It is also JD Logistics' controlling parent.
- Playtech (PTEC.L, graded buy now, 32.5%) did not hold up on competitive position: its own 10 November update warned 2027 will be tougher, with outside suppliers taking US share, the Brazil market shutdown and the UK gaming-duty rise, so 2026 is a peak-anchor year.
- Zealand Pharma (ZEAL.CO, graded buy now) did not hold up on competitive position: it has no recurring product revenue to show durable pricing power.
- Dave (DAVE, graded buy now) was repriced by the review from about $352 to $270 for undisclosed Connecticut and Maryland banking-regulator inquiries, which leaves the price above the repriced worth.
- PDD Holdings (graded buy now) carries a material correction: the review found its most load-bearing number misstated by 17% and re-marked the worth at $103.10; even on that figure the discount (about 31%) sits below the 35.0% bar, and it would be a fourth Consumer Cyclical name.
- PICC Group (1339.HK) was not killed but the review marked its anchor stale after a third-quarter loss of RMB 4.9 billion; it is a runner-up waiting for a full re-debate.

Correlation stress. Last run's measured correlations (two years of weekly returns) averaged 0.16 across pairs, with the highest pair Tencent Music and JD Logistics at 0.40 and no pair at or above 0.6 - these legs genuinely move apart in normal weeks; the clusters below are about the shared shock, not the week-to-week tape. Kia and SoftwareOne have no measured history with the book yet.
- Car-industry cycle - Duerr (DUE.DE), Inchcape (INCH.L), Kia (000270.KS). Kept, with a combined cap of 1.3 units (0.4 + 0.4 + 0.5). Duerr sells paint shops to carmakers, Inchcape sells their cars, Kia makes them: a global car recession hits all three. Kia is the most orthogonal way to add the week's best discount - Korean, net cash, no China overlap - which is why it was chosen over Geely; each leg is sized at or below half a unit so the three together are barely more than one full position.
- Interest-bearing borrowings and rates - Duerr (DUE.DE, cover about 0.6 times), Inchcape (INCH.L, about 2.4 times on GBP 2 billion of inventory funding) and SoftwareOne (SWON.SW, about 4 times on floating-rate loans). Kept with a combined cap of 1.2 units. In this tightening phase of the debt cycle, positive real long rates are being imposed and holding; all three pay more as rates stay high, which is why none is above 0.4 units.
- Consumer discretionary demand - Inchcape (INCH.L), Deckers (DECK), Kia (000270.KS). Kept with a combined cap of 1.4 units.
- US tariffs - Deckers (DECK, footwear made in Asia) and Kia (000270.KS, Korean exports under the new tariff regime). Kept with a combined cap of 1.0 unit.
- Chinese domestic demand and the yuan - Tencent Music (1698.HK) and JD Logistics (2618.HK), the book's most correlated pair. Kept with a combined cap of 0.9 units; this is the reason Geely and China Pacific Insurance stay runner-ups rather than becoming a third China leg. Both report on 17 November.
- UK economy and sterling - Inchcape (INCH.L) and Morgan Sindall (MGNS.L). Kept with a combined cap of 0.9 units; Inchcape earns mostly outside the UK, so the overlap is mainly the currency and the listing.
- Secular theme: AI displacement - Stride (LRN, AI search hurting enrollment leads) and Tencent Music (1698.HK, AI-generated music and content). Two names, the maximum the theme allows; neither has a wide moat, so neither counts at half. Kept with a combined cap of 0.9 units (secular-theme axis).
- Secular theme: labor-arbitrage deflation - SoftwareOne (SWON.SW) alone; no cluster.
- The standing pairs: Tenet and Universal Health (hospital reimbursement) - neither is seated, and Universal Health fails the price check. Comcast and Stroeer (advertising cycle) - neither is seated; Comcast is graded wait for proof. Pluxee and Euronet (payments disintermediation) - neither is seated; Pluxee carries the worsening-trajectory cap and its gap to Edenred is shared regulatory beta. Adobe, Gartner and Globant (AI displacement) - none is seated; Adobe's record is not a current view and Gartner is out on the forensic gate.
- Measured against the book: no hidden factor carries two full-size legs, and the largest single cluster (consumer discretionary) is capped at 1.4 of the book's 4.1 units.

Bear rebuttal - the strongest reason each pick is wrong, written before sizing:
- Duerr (DUE.DE): free cash flow has already turned negative, customer prepayments fell by about EUR 120 million in one quarter, and with interest cover under one times a further car-capex freeze could force the restructuring onto the balance sheet before the margin recovers.
- Inchcape (INCH.L): Asia-Pacific volumes are down about 37% and statutory profit is falling faster than the adjusted figure, so the 930-pence worth may be anchored on a margin that the distribution model can no longer earn.
- Kia (000270.KS): the net cash may be permanently trapped by Korean governance, the US tariff is a lasting cost, and an unexplained collapse in below-the-line income could be the first sign of an affiliate problem.
- JD Logistics (2618.HK): its biggest customer is its controlling parent, which sets the prices, so the minority holder may never see the margin the valuation assumes.
- SoftwareOne (SWON.SW): Microsoft keeps cutting partner incentives and moving customers to direct cloud contracts, so a reseller with falling returns and floating-rate debt may be a melting ice cube that only looks cheap on adjusted profit.
- Deckers (DECK): HOKA growth has slowed to low single digits and a fashion brand can de-rate permanently once it stops growing.
- Stride (LRN): enrollment is falling and AI-driven search is cutting new-student leads, so the worth assumes a stabilisation the business has not yet shown.
- Tencent Music (1698.HK): growth has slowed to about 6% and the debt-funded Ximalaya purchase dilutes margins, so the 17 November print could confirm a low-growth platform worth less than HK$43.
- Morgan Sindall (MGNS.L): the fit-out margin is at a cycle high and the stock trades within about 9% of its worth, so the remaining upside is small against a downside to 3,345 pence.

Rotation, reconciled to the value ledger:
- KEEP Duerr (DUE.DE): held since 24 August 2026 at EUR 17.32, now EUR 16.40 - graded wait for a better price, not a buy here; adds near EUR 15.
- KEEP Inchcape (INCH.L): held since 13 October 2026 at 674.5 pence, now 651 pence - graded buy now after today's full re-debate (worth 930 pence, taking in the second model's repricing from 950).
- KEEP JD Logistics (2618.HK): held since 20 October 2026 at HK$10.26, now HK$10.27 - graded buy now after today's full re-debate (worth cut to HK$13.86, taking in the second model's repricing).
- KEEP Deckers (DECK): held since 3 November 2026 at $84.09, now $86.82 - graded buy now, but held on its margin of safety alone and cut to 0.5 units because its downside case now sits close to the price.
- KEEP Stride (LRN): held since 10 August 2026 at $82.51, now $75.82 - graded wait for proof, not a buy here; adds only once the late-January fiscal second-quarter results show enrollment of 243,000 or more with the operating-income guide held at $505 million or more.
- KEEP Tencent Music (1698.HK): held since 31 August 2026 at HK$34.12, now HK$34.98 - graded wait for proof, not a buy here; adds only once the 17 November third-quarter results show revenue growth of 5% or more, gross margin within about 1.5 points of last year and net cash intact.
- KEEP Morgan Sindall (MGNS.L): held since 27 October 2026 at 4,054 pence, now 4,510 pence - graded wait for a better price and above its trim line, not a buy here; adds only near 4,129 pence.
- ADD Kia (000270.KS): never held; graded buy now at 94,600 won on a full debate seven days old, all five models cheap, about 30% below its 135,000-won worth.
- ADD SoftwareOne (SWON.SW): never held; graded buy now at CHF 8.72 on a full debate dated today, about 27% below the review-checked CHF 11.89 worth, seated on the margin of safety alone at 0.4 units.
- 4 of 9 seats are wait-graded: held, not a buy at today's price - Duerr and Morgan Sindall wait for a better price, Stride and Tencent Music wait for proof at their dated results.
- No held name was dropped and nothing was re-added; none of the 43 names dropped this year returns.

Rise and fall against the prior book (10 November): all seven names carry over. Duerr's discount narrowed from 48% to 45% as the price recovered; Inchcape from 49% to 43% (worth trimmed to 930 pence, price up to 651); JD Logistics from 39% to 35% (worth cut to HK$13.86); Stride from 30% to 29%; Deckers is unchanged at 29% but loses a quarter unit on its thin downside case; Tencent Music widened from 15% to 23% as the price fell back below its trim line; Morgan Sindall narrowed from 14% to 10% as the price rose. Kia and SoftwareOne are new.

Kia CRO-only check: not applicable - all five models agree. SoftwareOne is the book's one CRO-only leg (two of five models positive, raw screen at 0%): the five models run on reported net income that is near zero after merger costs and acquisition amortisation, so they cannot see a merged business earning about a 24% adjusted margin on CHF 100 million of realised savings, which the sum-of-the-parts values on operating earnings instead; for that reason it is held to 0.4 units.

Secular load. The share of the book exposed to structural decline is 55.6% (5 of 9 seats carry a material secular threat or an eroding moat: Duerr, Inchcape, Kia, Tencent Music and SoftwareOne), below the 60% line. Clean anchors - a real moat, a stable or widening trend and a manageable threat - number 4: JD Logistics, Deckers, Stride and Morgan Sindall.
